**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after its parents #1002 and #1019; see merge order).

Reviewed at the effort:high tier (posted G-code, safety floor), trial-merged with current `upstream/main` (clean, no conflicts).

### What looks good
- Stack is as stated: `b471395e` (#1002) -> `321df394`/`25cbac81` (#1019, current head 25cbac81) -> `c5e931c6` + `c12b4d16` (this PR). Nothing else rides along.
- The away seat now follows the verified hop: up to `max(RetractPlane, R)` when below it, XY across, then down to R only if above R. A tool already above the hop traverses where it stands; an unknown start (`StartZ` absent) climbs first (conservative). Never a straight line through stock or clamps. The cycle is emitted only after the seat; an open group is closed with `G80` first (existing `cycleSeat` path).
- No `RetractPlane` stated: refused by name ("a canned cycle is read away from its hole with no rapid to it, and the section states no RetractPlane to traverse at"). `hopZ` is captured in `onParameter` and cleared in `onSectionEnd`, so a section cannot borrow the previous operation's hop.
- `probeSeat()` sets `seatKnown` and closes an open group with `G80` in `onProbeMove`, `onProbeRetreat` and `onProbeGuard`, in all six posts (tormach has the three functions in a different order in the file; each is covered; doosan's covers the Renishaw path through `onProbeMove`).
- Six posts are consistent: I diffed each `.cps` hunk against fanuc's. mazak and doosan-dnm are textually identical to fanuc; haas, sinumerik and tormach differ only in the dialect's `G0` vs `G00` spelling. Heidenhain and Carvera (expanded chain) and fanuc-lathe (#1042 area) are untouched.
- Pinned by `cycle_hop` (7 tests, all six posts through the checker), including refusal-by-name and the probing case; the PR body documents a revert check for each fix separately.
- Goldens, line by line (compared with #1019's head): `synth_fanuc`, `synth_haas`, `synth_mazak`, `synth_tormach`, `synth_doosan-dnm` each gain, before each of the 5 cycle holes, `G0(0) Z0` (hop: RetractPlane 5 less OriginZ 5) and, after the XY traverse, `G0(0) Z-3` (R=2 less 5), and the old pre-XY `Z-3` of the first hole becomes `Z0`; nothing else moves. `synth_sinumerik` is the same plus renumbered N words (I stripped the N words and compared: only the 5 pairs of `G0 Z0`/`G0 Z-3` and the shifted tail differ). Heidenhain/Carvera goldens unchanged. The only test-source change is the fixture stating `ClearancePlane 10` / `RetractPlane 5` in `conformance.rs`, which is what a generator writes. No other golden in this PR's own diff.
- Law check: no snapshot PNGs, no CHANGELOG.md edit, no process-file change (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md` is not one, so no PROCESS_VERSION bump needed), decision file `docs/decisions/1028-cycle-seat-latent.md`, body ends `Fixes #1028` with a `Changelog:` line, conventional subjects, no build.rs/.github/scripts/dependency changes. `.cps` scripts are exempt from the 400-line rule.

### Local results (worktree own `target/`, sccache, merged with upstream/main)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| post: lib 16, cycle_hop 7, recorded_streams 10, post_engine 33, comp 9, comp_plane 3, mch_head_search 2, axis_direction_cli 3, each of the 10 `script_*` suites 9 | all ok |
| app: posting 17, golden_cl 25, conformance 6, drilling_axial 7, drill_prior 12, drill_rplane 8, recorded_post_streams 2 | ok |
| app: fanuc_post 11, tormach_post 10, doosan_dnm_post 7, inverted_post 15, probe_dialects 13, probe_tormach 7, probe_guard 5, inverted_probe 9 | ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Merge order
Merge-tree of this head against #1019, #1002, #1025 and #1042 is clean for each (no conflicts). Order: #1002, then #1019, then this PR; retarget is not needed (all three target main) but this PR's diff shrinks to its own two commits once the parents land. #1025 and #1042 (fanuc-lathe) are independent of it and can go in any order.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- Not exercised on a real control, as the PR says; Doosan's Renishaw G65 probe path has no machine-enabled test.
- A section with an unstated `RetractPlane` and back-to-back cycle records now refuses; any hand-written stream test elsewhere that relied on the old straight traverse would fail loudly, and I found none across the suites above.
- `crates/post/tests/cycle_hop.rs` has grown by ~390 lines in this PR (and is well over 400); consider splitting the probe-checker tests out later.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Merge order: #1002, then #1019, then this PR. Retarget each child PR to `main` before its parent merges.

I built and tested this PR together with #1019 and #1002 in one worktree: this head trial-merged with current `main` (`a6bd69d8`). The merge was clean. I judged only this PR's own commits, `c5e931c6` and `c12b4d16`.

### What looks good
- **Identical in all six posts.** The post change is the same in fanuc, haas, mazak, tormach, doosan-dnm and sinumerik; only the `G0` / `G00` spelling differs. I checked this by comparing the non-comment diff lines of each post.
- **Seat height.** A cycle read away from its hole is seated at `max(RetractPlane, R)`:
  - it climbs first when the tool is below that height, or when its Z is unknown (`StartZ` missing means the post climbs);
  - it then traverses to the cycle's own `X Y`, then drops to R.

  The seat can't run lower than the section's hop, which is the plane the verified links use. It can't pick the wrong hole, because the XY comes from the cycle record itself. A tool already above the hop traverses where it stands, which is higher still.
- **No hop stated.** With no `RetractPlane` in the section, the seat is refused by name and no R-level guess is made. `hopZ` is reset at section end, so one operation never borrows another's hop.
- **Probing.** `probeSeat()` runs on touch, retreat and guard moves:
  - it marks the position as known, so a later cycle is seated from the tracked position and never from an assumed one;
  - it closes any open group with `G80` before the probe block.
- **Modal state.** `G99` is still written when each group opens. Every seat path writes `G80` before it moves. A seat that stays over the hole (only up or down to R) behaves as in #1019.
- **Goldens: all six `synth_*` diffs read line by line.** Each hole gains `G0(0) Z0` (the hop: 5 world minus origin Z 5) before its XY traverse and `G0(0) Z-3` (R) after it, where before the traverse ran at R. Sinumerik's other lines only change N numbers. No GOTO or sub-program target appears in these files. `synth_heidenhain` and `synth_carvera` are unchanged.
- **Conformance fixture.** The only change in `conformance.rs` is two `PARAM`s in `synth_stream_with` (`ClearancePlane 10`, `RetractPlane 5`, as in the recorded `drill_retract`). No assertion was touched or weakened.
- **Checker.** The `cycle_hop` checker only gains reach: G31 / G38.n read as straight moves, G91 back-offs are tracked, and `from_start` watches every traverse from the first known position. Its existing fault conditions are unchanged.
- The four new tests pin both gaps, each with a revert check (in the PR body). The decision file is present, the code is clean-room (RS-274 / ISO 6983 only), and there is no `unwrap` / `panic!` outside tests.

| clippy `-D warnings`: `-p camcraft-post --all-targets`, and `-p camcraft-app` lib + conformance / posting / doosan_dnm_post / inverted_post / recorded_post_streams | clean |

App suites with test counts: conformance 6, posting 17, golden_cl 25, fanuc_post 11, doosan_dnm_post 7, tormach_post 10, tormach_machines 6, tormach_end_units 7, probe_dialects 13, probe_tormach 7, probe_guard 5, probe_report 5, probe_op 12, probe_spindle_stop 2, drill_rplane 8, drill_prior 12, drill_prior_kinds 4, drilling_axial 7, tapping_mode 4, tap_sim 2, inverted_post 15, inverted_probe 9, inverted_equivalence 2, sinumerik_safe_retract 3, tormach_safe_retract 4, program_comments 4, heidenhain_cycles 11, setup_post_options 10, recorded_post_streams 2.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
- **How the refusal blocks.** The no-hop refusal is a counted warning (`msg`), and the post still writes the cycle block after it. The in-app gate blocks on that warning, as for the other named refusals. A command-line user of the `post` binary would still get a program plus the warning.
- **Doosan probing path.** The Renishaw G65 path in doosan-dnm goes through the same `probeSeat()`, but no test enables it, as the body says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
